source: read by eye off tools/grid_crop.py zooms + row intensity profiles, 2026-09-26 (Claude). Pixels are in the REFERENCE view that stabilize_park.py maps every clip into.

points.name: plate_center
points.note: centre of the white plate bar, cols 736-794 on row 416 (3 px tall: the whole plate seen edge-on). World y = 12 in, mid-depth of the 17 in wide part

widths_px.note: NOT used in the fit: plate 58 px / 17 in = 3.4 px/in vs rubber 64 px / 24 in = 2.7 px/in, which no camera behind the rubber can produce. One of the two widths is not what it looks like (rubber partly buried / plate bar includes chalk). Centres are robust to that; widths are not.

features.foul: white-chalk foul-line samples (px), both lines, far from the plate only (x<505 or x>=1000); near the plate the chalk is mixed with batter's-box lines
features.mound: dirt/grass boundary of the 9 ft radius mound circle centred (0, 59, 0), pitcher and scorebug excluded
features.plate_ends: ends of the white plate bar, row 416, cols 736 and 794 = (+-8.5 in, ~12 in, 0)

rejected.rubber_slab: The white ribbed slab at (528-592, 654-677) is NOT the rubber. It is 64 px wide where the mound implies a 24 in rubber is ~105 px, and the ground-landmark camera projects the raised rubber (z = 10 in) to y 621 -- exactly under the pitcher's feet, who is standing on it at set-up. The slab sits behind the rubber, lower. Kept here so nobody re-marks it.

overlay_note: scorebug, masked from homography matching (the v1 ORB stabilization locked onto it)
